customManagers.description: OpenBao versions, its KMS seal plugins, and node_exporter, wherever an OpenBao node is configured: both clouds' cluster stacks and the restore drill. The flux/helm-values/kubernetes managers all ignore `opentofu`, and the terraform manager does not look at variable defaults, so these were bumped by hand - node_exporter had been pinned to a July 2024 release since it was written. The drill and the GCP startup script were added on 2026-09-26: #2095 bumped the clusters to 2.7.0 and left the drill on 2.6.2, because nothing here matched its `BAO_VERSION:` line. Plugin images carry tag and digest, and Renovate updates both.

Bootstrap chart versions in opentofu/config.tm.hcl (Cilium, flux-operator, flux-instance). The flux, helm-values and kubernetes managers all ignore `opentofu`, and the terraform manager does not read Terramate globals, so these were bumped by hand: on 2026-09-26 Cilium sat on 1.20.1 ten days after 1.20.2 and flux-operator on 0.59.0 fifteen days after 0.60.0, while Renovate automerged everything it could see. Each pin carries a `# renovate:` comment on the line above; `registryUrl` is optional because the OCI charts resolve through the docker datasource by their full name.

Pinned tool versions in container-images/**/Dockerfile ARGs. Otherwise bumped by hand, same as the openbao_version entry above - GCLOUD_VERSION is deliberately left unannotated there (see the Dockerfile comment): it's an apt package version from Google's own repo, not a GitHub release, and Renovate has no datasource for it.

Grafana datasource plugin pins inside the vm-common-helm-values ConfigMap. They live in a quoted values.yaml string as '<id>@<version>' entries (the chart's GF_PLUGINS_PREINSTALL_SYNC pin separator), invisible to the flux/helm-values managers; the VM plugin sat frozen at v0.14.0 for 16 months because of this.

packageRules.description: Automerge patch and minor updates once CI is green. The gate is the six required `ci.yaml` checks and nothing else: GitHub's native auto-merge (repo setting `allow_auto_merge`, turned on 2026-09-12) squash-merges the PR the moment the last one reports success, and it still honours branch protection in full — so `enforce_admins` and the conversation-resolution requirement apply exactly as they do to a hand-merged PR. Majors are deliberately excluded and keep waiting for a human. This DOES include 0.x minors, where semver-minor is routinely a breaking change (chart 0.2 → 0.3 restructuring its values schema is the local scar, see the semantic-router rule below): a deliberate call, on the grounds that `validate-manifests.sh` renders and validates the whole tree on every PR and both clusters are rebuildable. When a specific 0.x package proves it cannot be trusted, bound it with `allowedVersions` the way the two rules below do, rather than narrowing this one.

Never automerge the Grafana plugin pins, whatever the update type. They are TRACKED from GitHub releases and INSTALLED from the Grafana.com catalog, and the two publish independently — a tag can exist on GitHub days before, or without ever, reaching the catalog. Renovate has no catalog datasource, so it cannot tell the difference: a bump to a version the catalog does not carry is green on every check here and CrashLoopBackOff on the cluster, because the plugin installer is a startup module and Grafana refuses to start rather than start without the plugin. That takes observability -> tooling -> apps down with it. It has already happened twice — #1959 reverted by #1980, #1981 reverted by #1982 — and #1980 pinned the version back with the check to run recorded in the ConfigMap at the point someone is next asked to accept a bump: `curl -s https://grafana.com/api/plugins/<plugin-id>/versions`. Automerging would mean nobody is ever asked, and that comment would go unread. Matched by file rather than by package so a third plugin added to the same list inherits the exclusion for free.

Block the 0.3.x schema break, not the whole chart. Chart 0.3.0 restructures the values schema (canonical-v0.3 providers/routing/global); our values still speak 0.2, so the chart's own 0.3 component defaults win — including pullPolicy: Never, which breaks the router on any fresh node (ErrImageNeverPull -> every `model: MoM` request 404s). Renovate bumped this past a plain code comment (c00892eb) and it stayed invisible for five weeks, because running clusters kept already-pulled images. allowedVersions rather than enabled:false so 0.2.x patch and security releases still flow. Lift the bound in the same PR that migrates infrastructure/base/vllm-semantic-router/helmrelease.yaml to the 0.3 schema.

Hold the google providers at v7 until the CFT modules allow v8. terraform-google-modules/kubernetes-engine (44.3.0) and .../network (18.1.2) are both already the LATEST releases, and both constrain the provider to < 8.0.0, so a v8 bump here is not merely risky -- it is unsatisfiable, and `tofu init` refuses outright: "Could not resolve provider hashicorp/google: no available releases match the given constraints ... ~> 8.0, < 8.0.0". Renovate opened #1854 and #1855 for it anyway and both failed CI, because nothing in a version constraint tells Renovate what the modules require. Lift this bound in the same PR that bumps those two modules to releases supporting provider v8.

Hold the Headlamp plugin's TypeScript below 7. typescript-eslint, pulled in through @headlamp-k8s/eslint-config, refuses TS 7 ("typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0"), so the image build fails at `npm run lint` and never reaches the compiler. Renovate opened #2032 for it anyway. Lift this bound once typescript-eslint supports TS >= 7: https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/10940

Never automerge a GitHub Action digest bump. Every `uses:` in this repo is pinned to a commit SHA, which is what makes a retagged action -- the tj-actions/changed-files compromise, CVE-2025-30066, where every tag including version tags was moved to a commit that dumped runner memory into the build log -- a visible diff rather than a silent substitution. That property only holds while a human looks at the new SHA. Automerging digest updates would restore the old behaviour exactly, with a PR trail as the only difference. Stated as its own rule rather than relying on `digest` being absent from the patch/minor automerge list above, so widening that list cannot undo this by accident. `minimumReleaseAge` is the second half: a malicious retag is typically caught within hours, so not proposing one for three days means the usual attack is revoked before it is ever offered here.

One PR per Upjet provider family. The members (provider-aws-iam, -ec2, -eks, -kms, -s3) share one provider-family-aws and are released in lockstep; one PR per member would run the cluster on mixed member versions between merges. The 2026-09-26 bump from v2.6.0 to v2.8.1 moved all five at once for that reason.
Same as the provider-aws family rule, for the GCP members.

Never bump our own Configuration packages. The App Wizard clones the same crossplane-configuration tag through a `--branch=` argument in apps/platform/app-wizard/app.yaml that no manager can see, and infrastructure/AGENTS.md requires the two to move together. A Renovate PR would move only the package, and the wizard would render against the old compositions.

Hold function-kcl below v0.12.3. That release only bumps dependencies, including the KCL runtime, yet rendering the InferenceService composition with it drops the leading space of a `""" --revision """` fragment, so the preload Job runs `hf download Qwen/Qwen3-8B--revision main` and no base model ever downloads. The golden renders in Smana/crossplane-configuration caught it (16/20 match; v0.12.2 renders 20/20), which is also why that repo's functions.yaml must move in lockstep with this one. Lift this bound in the same PR that bumps both, once main.k builds that command without depending on whitespace inside a triple-quoted string, and the goldens match on the new version.

OpenBao and its KMS seal plugins: one PR, never automerged. CI never boots an OpenBao node, so a green PR proves nothing about whether the server starts. #2095 (2.6.2 -> 2.7.0, automerged 2026-09-25) removed the built-in awskms seal, and the next deploy died with "unknown wrapper: awskms". The weekly restore drill is the only automated boot, and it runs after the merge. Grouped because a server version and its seal plugin must be compatible.
